text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- New crisis hits Nigerian oil industry as department of petroleum resources staff who document crude oil exports start work-to-rule to back demand for payment of salary arrears.
- Federal government sends delegation led by Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi to Liberia to assess preparations for elections scheduled there for May 30, 1997.
- Mass arrests in troubled oil city of Warri as police launch counter-attack to defend themselves in communal riots there. Shell oil company says oil production going on smoothly.
- The federal government may draft soldiers to quell communal clashes in Warri in the midwest if it agrees to the recomendation of the local military governor.
- Nigeria is one of 10 sub-Saharan African nations to benefit from a grant of $10.2 million from the United Nations Development Fund to enable them to get connected to the internet.
- Task force on revenue generation seals off premises of some firms in Lagos in a bid to recover taxes due to Lagos state government.
- British-American Tobacco (BAT) may announce its withdrawal from Nigerian Tobacco Company when the later holds its annual general meeting in Abuja Thursday, company sources say.
- Election of state governors scheduled for the last quarter of this year under Nigeria's return to democracy programme may be shifted to next year, political sources say.
- Demand for treasury bills drops at latest weekly sale of the debt instrument, says central bank.
